question: Effect of a predominantly balanced versus predominantly 0.9% saline crystalloid strategy over the first 24 h of ICU on chloride at ~24 h
data: eICU Collaborative Research Database 2.0 (eICU is development data for the forecasting line; this causal analysis is new and no outcome of it has been read)
target_trial: see eicu_crystalloid_iv_extract.py docstring (eligibility, strategies, time zero, instrument, outcome windows)
estimator: 2SLS, frozen covariate set crystalloid_iv_design.covariate_matrix, hospital cluster bootstrap 1,000 replicates, seed 0
readiness_rules: see crystalloid_iv_estimate.py docstring: F >= 10; |SMD| <= 0.10 across instrument halves; outcome availability gap <= 0.05; benchmark chloride estimate in [-8, -0.3] mmol/L with CI upper < 0; placebo (baseline chloride) CI contains 0; negative control (platelet change) CI contains 0; external review required
benchmark_source: Xue et al., Ann Intensive Care 2019 (8 RCTs, 19,301 patients): balanced crystalloids reduce the rise in serum chloride, SMD -1.23 (95% CI -1.59 to -0.87); no consistent bicarbonate/pH difference
one_shot_rule: outcomes are extracted once after this freeze and analysed once; only crashes may be fixed, each reported
